ei.title: Mirror Neurons and Learning by Observation
ei.subject: 9월_2024 고1 모의고사
ei.lesson: Mirror Neurons and Learning by Observation

fullPassage: The discovery of mirror neurons has profoundly changed the way we think of a fundamental human capacity, learning by observation. As children we learn a lot by observing what our parents and friends do. Newborns, in the first week of life, have an inborn tendency to stick out their tongue if their parents stick out theirs. Such imitation is not perfect. You may not see the tongue stick out each time you stick yours out at your newborn, but if you do it many times, the tongue will come out more often than if you do something different. Babies babble and later start to imitate the sounds their parents produce. Later still, they play with vacuum cleaners and hammers in imitation of their parents. Our modern cultures, in which we write, speak, read, build spaceships and go to school, can work only because we are not restricted to the behavior we are born with or learn by trial and error. We can learn a lot by simply watching others.

questions.passage: The discovery of mirror neurons has profoundly changed the way we think of a (A)[trivial / fundamental] human capacity, learning by observation. As children we learn a lot by observing what our parents and friends do. Newborns, in the first week of life, have an (B)[inborn / acquired] tendency to stick out their tongue if their parents stick out theirs. Such imitation is not perfect. You may not see the tongue stick out each time you stick yours out at your newborn, but if you do it many times, the tongue will come out more often than if you do something different. Babies babble and later start to (C)[ignore / imitate] the sounds their parents produce. Later still, they play with vacuum cleaners and hammers in imitation of their parents. Our modern cultures, in which we write, speak, read, build spaceships and go to school, can work only because we are not restricted to the behavior we are born with or learn by trial and error. We can learn a lot by simply watching others.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) fundamental=근본적인, (B) inborn=타고난, (C) imitate=모방하다
det.analysis:
✅ ① fundamental — inborn — imitate: 원문 일치. 관찰 학습은 '근본적인(fundamental)' 인간 능력이고, 신생아는 '타고난(inborn)' 경향을 가지며, 아기는 소리를 '모방한다(imitate)'는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ② trivial — inborn — imitate: (A) trivial(사소한)은 fundamental(근본적인)의 반의어로 부적절
❌ ③ fundamental — acquired — imitate: (B) acquired(후천적으로 얻은)는 inborn(타고난)의 반의어로 부적절
❌ ④ fundamental — inborn — ignore: (C) ignore(무시하다)는 imitate(모방하다)의 반의어로 부적절
det.tip: fundamental human capacity(근본적 능력) / inborn tendency(타고난 경향) / imitate the sounds(소리를 모방)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) profoundly=깊이, (B) observing=관찰하는 것, (C) restricted=제한된
det.analysis:
❌ ① profoundly — ignoring — restricted: (B) ignoring(무시하는 것)은 observing(관찰하는 것)의 반의어로 부적절
❌ ② slightly — observing — restricted: (A) slightly(약간)는 profoundly(깊이)의 반의어로 부적절
✅ ③ profoundly — observing — restricted: 원문 일치. 거울 뉴런의 발견이 '깊이(profoundly)' 바꿨고, '관찰함으로써(observing)' 배우며, 우리는 타고난 행동에 '제한되지(restricted)' 않는다는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ④ profoundly — observing — encouraged: (C) encouraged(장려된)는 restricted(제한된)의 반의어 방향으로 부적절
det.tip: profoundly changed(깊이 바꿈) / by observing(관찰함으로써) / not restricted(제한되지 않음)

questions.passage: The discovery of mirror neurons has profoundly changed the way we think of a fundamental human capacity, learning by observation. As children we learn a lot by observing what our parents and friends do. Newborns, in the first week of life, have an inborn tendency to stick out their tongue if their parents stick out theirs. Such imitation is not (A)[flawed / perfect]. You may not see the tongue stick out each time you stick yours out at your newborn, but if you do it many times, the tongue will come out more often than if you do something different. Babies babble and later start to imitate the sounds their parents (B)[produce / consume]. Later still, they play with vacuum cleaners and hammers in imitation of their parents. Our modern cultures, in which we write, speak, read, build spaceships and go to school, can work only because we are not restricted to the behavior we are born with or learn by trial and error. questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) perfect=완벽한, (B) produce=만들어내다, (C) simply=단순히
det.analysis:
❌ ① flawed — produce — simply: (A) flawed(결함 있는)는 perfect(완벽한)의 반의어로 부적절
❌ ② perfect — consume — simply: (B) consume(소비하다)은 produce(만들어내다)의 반의어로 부적절
❌ ③ perfect — produce — hardly: (C) hardly(거의 ~않는)는 simply(단순히)의 의미와 상충되어 부적절
✅ ④ perfect — produce — simply: 원문 일치. 모방은 '완벽하지(perfect)' 않고, 부모가 소리를 '만들어내며(produce)', 단지 '단순히(simply)' 봄으로써 배운다는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
det.tip: not perfect(완벽하지 않은) / parents produce(부모가 만들어냄) / simply watching(단순히 봄)

Babies babble and later start to ④<u>imitate</u> the sounds their parents produce. Later still, they play with vacuum cleaners and hammers in imitation of their parents. Our modern cultures, in which we write, speak, read, build spaceships and go to school, can work only because we are not restricted to the behavior we are born with or learn by trial and error. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: learned → inborn: 신생아가 태어날 때부터 가진 '타고난(inborn)' 경향이라는 맥락에서 learned(학습된)는 부적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① discovery — 원문 일치. 거울 뉴런의 '발견(discovery)'이라는 맥락에 적절
❌ ② observing — 원문 일치. 부모가 하는 것을 '관찰함(observing)'으로써 배운다는 맥락에 적절
✅ ③ learned — 원문은 inborn(타고난). 생후 첫 주 신생아의 경향은 태어날 때부터 지닌 것이므로 learned(학습된)는 모순 ←정답
❌ ④ imitate — 원문 일치. 부모의 소리를 '모방한다(imitate)'는 맥락에 적절
det.tip: inborn tendency(타고난 경향) — learned(학습된)는 정반대

questions.passage: The discovery of mirror neurons has ①<u>profoundly</u> changed the way we think of a fundamental human capacity, learning by observation. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: flawed → perfect: 모방이 '완벽하지(perfect)' 않다는 맥락에서 flawed(결함 있는)로 바꾸면 '결함이 없다'가 되어 뒤 예시와 모순
det.analysis:
❌ ① profoundly — 원문 일치. 사고방식을 '깊이(profoundly)' 바꿨다는 맥락에 적절
❌ ② parents — 원문 일치. 우리 '부모(parents)'가 하는 것을 관찰한다는 맥락에 적절
✅ ③ flawed — 원문은 perfect(완벽한). 'Such imitation is not perfect(모방은 완벽하지 않다)'인데 flawed로 바꾸면 'not flawed(결함이 없다)'가 되어 이어지는 불완전 예시와 모순 ←정답
❌ ④ produce — 원문 일치. 부모가 만들어내는 소리를 '만들어낸다(produce)'는 맥락에 적절
det.tip: imitation is not perfect(모방은 완벽하지 않음) — flawed로 바꾸면 의미 뒤집힘

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: identical → different: 부모와 '다른(different)' 행동을 하면 혀가 덜 나온다는 맥락에서 identical(똑같은)은 부적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① observing — 원문 일치. 부모를 '관찰함(observing)'으로써 배운다는 맥락에 적절
✅ ② identical — 원문은 different(다른). '혀 내밀기를 많이 하면 something different(다른 것)를 할 때보다 혀가 더 자주 나온다'는 대조인데 identical(똑같은)로 바꾸면 대조가 무너져 부적절 ←정답
❌ ③ babble — 원문 일치. 아기들이 '옹알이한다(babble)'는 맥락에 적절
❌ ④ restricted — 원문 일치. 타고난 행동에 '제한되지(restricted)' 않는다는 맥락에 적절
det.tip: something different(다른 것)와의 대조 — identical(똑같은)은 대조를 깨뜨림

det.korean: 부모와 친구가 하는 것을 '관찰함(observing)'으로써 많이 배운다는 맥락
det.analysis:

❌ ② ideal — 이상적인(ideal)은 perfect와 유사
❌ ③ flawless — 흠 없는(flawless)은 perfect와 동의어
✅ ④ flawed — perfect의 반의어. '결함 있는'은 '완벽한'의 정반대 ←정답
det.tip: perfect(완벽한) ↔ flawed(결함 있는)

questions.passage: The discovery of mirror neurons has profoundly changed the way we think of a fundamental human capacity, learning by observation. As children we learn a lot by observing what our parents and friends do. Newborns, in the first week of life, have an <u>inborn</u> tendency to stick out their tongue if their parents stick out theirs. Such imitation is not perfect. You may not see the tongue stick out each time you stick yours out at your newborn, but if you do it many times, the tongue will come out more often than if you do something different. Babies babble and later start to imitate the sounds their parents produce. Later still, they play with vacuum cleaners and hammers in imitation of their parents. Our modern cultures, in which we write, speak, read, build spaceships and go to school, can work only because we are not restricted to the behavior we are born with or learn by trial and error. We can learn a lot by simply watching others.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 inborn의 의미와 가장 먼 것은?

det.korean: inborn=타고난 ↔ acquired=후천적으로 얻은
det.analysis:
❌ ① innate — 타고난(innate)은 inborn과 동의어
❌ ② natural — 자연적인/선천적인(natural)은 inborn과 유사
❌ ③ inherent — 내재된(inherent)은 inborn과 유사
✅ ④ acquired — inborn의 반의어. '후천적으로 얻은'은 '타고난'의 정반대 ←정답
det.tip: inborn(타고난) ↔ acquired(후천적으로 얻은)

questions.passage:
(A) The new factory can produce thousands of cars every month for the growing market. Engineers there work hard to produce goods of high quality.

(B) At the farmers' market, she bought fresh produce such as tomatoes, carrots, and lettuce. The produce looked colorful and had been picked that very morning.
questions.stem: 다음 (A)와 (B)에서 밑줄 친 produce의 문맥적 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) produce=생산하다(동사), (B) produce=농산물(명사)
det.analysis:
✅ ① (A) 생산하다 — (B) 농산물: (A)에서 produce는 공장이 자동차를 '생산하다'라는 동사이고, (B)에서 produce는 시장에서 파는 '농산물'이라는 명사 ←정답
❌ ② (A) 농산물 — (B) 생산하다: 두 의미가 뒤바뀜
❌ ③ (A) 공연하다 — (B) 생산량: 두 문맥 모두 부적절
❌ ④ (A) 제시하다 — (B) 결과물: 두 문맥 모두 부적절
det.tip: produce: 생산하다(동사) / 농산물(명사) — 다의어

questions.stem:
다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?
"the act of copying the behavior, speech, or actions of someone else"

det.korean: 다른 사람의 행동·말·동작을 따라 하는 행위 → imitation(모방)
det.analysis:
❌ ① observation — 관찰(observation)은 '지켜보는 것'이지 '따라 하는 것'이 아님
✅ ② imitation — '다른 사람의 행동·말을 따라 하는 행위'라는 정의에 정확히 부합 ←정답
❌ ③ discovery — 발견(discovery)은 정의와 무관
❌ ④ restriction — 제한(restriction)은 정의와 무관
det.tip: imitation = copying someone else's behavior/speech

questions.passage: As children we learn a lot by __________ (observe) what our parents and friends do. We can learn a lot by simply watching others.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오.

det.korean: observe → observing: 전치사 by 뒤에는 동명사가 와야 함
det.analysis: ✅ 정답: observing — 'learn a lot by _____(observe)'에서 전치사 by 뒤에는 동명사(-ing)가 필요하므로 observe → observing
det.tip: by + 동명사(observing) = ~함으로써

questions.passage: Later still, they play with vacuum cleaners and hammers in __________ (imitate) of their parents.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오.

det.korean: imitate → imitation: 전치사 in과 of 사이에는 명사가 필요. in imitation of = ~을 모방하여
det.analysis: ✅ 정답: imitation — 'in _____(imitate) of their parents'에서 전치사 in과 of 사이에는 명사가 와야 하므로 동사 imitate를 명사 imitation으로 변형
det.tip: in imitation of ~ (~을 모방하여) = 명사형

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 거울 뉴런의 발견이 바꾼 근본적 인간 능력은 '관찰에 의한 학습(learning by observation)'이라는 맥락
det.analysis:
✅ ① learning by observation — 원문 일치. 뒤 문장들이 모두 '관찰·모방을 통한 학습'을 설명하므로 '관찰에 의한 학습'이 적절 ←정답
❌ ② teaching by instruction — 지시에 의한 가르침은 관찰 학습이라는 글 전체 주제와 반대
❌ ③ competing for rewards — 보상을 위한 경쟁은 본문과 무관
❌ ④ memorizing by repetition — 반복 암기는 관찰 학습과 다른 개념
det.tip: a fundamental human capacity = learning by observation(관찰 학습)

det.korean: 우리가 타고나거나 '시행착오(trial and error)'로 배운 행동에만 제한되지 않는다는 맥락

✅ ④ trial and error — 원문 일치. 'born with or learn by _____'에서 시행착오로 배운다가 적절 ←정답
det.tip: learn by trial and error — 시행착오로 배움
